How much does water heater replacement cost?

Swapping the tank — or going tankless — what it costs, and what moves the price:

$882–$1,826

National average $1,348

Bay Area: $1,246–$2,342 (avg $1,753) — roughly 30% above the national average.

Why quotes run $900 to $6,000

Unit type
Tank: $900–$2,500. Tankless: $1,400–$5,600. Heat-pump hybrid: $2,500–$6,000.
Size & fuel
Tanks run 30–80 gallons; gas vs. electric changes the install. Bigger households need bigger tanks.
Venting & lines
Switching types often means new venting, a bigger gas line, or electrical work — plus bringing everything up to code.
Access
A garage swap is the easy case. Tight closets, attics, and crawl spaces add labor hours.
Unit choice

Tank vs. tankless

Tank
$900–$2,500

The cheapest straightforward swap. Lasts 8–12 years. Hot water runs out; standby heat costs you every month.

Tankless
$1,400–$5,600

Endless hot water, 20+ year life, no standby loss. Needs a bigger gas line or serious electrical — that’s where the premium goes.

Bottom line: tank for the cheapest swap today; tankless if you’ll be in the house long enough to earn the premium back.

Common questions

How long do water heaters last?

Tank models: 8–12 years. Tankless: 20 years or more. Hard water shortens both — a softener or an annual flush helps.

Tank or tankless?

Tankless for endless hot water and a 20+ year life, if the upfront cost and the gas or electrical upgrades work for you. Tank for the cheapest like-for-like swap.

How long does replacement take?

A few hours for a like-for-like tank swap. Most of a day when switching types or rerouting venting and lines.

Do I need a permit?

Most Bay Area cities require one for water heater swaps. Installers usually pull it as part of the job.
